hints.title: Key Insight and Observation
hints.text: In a circular sequence of length n, the total number of adjacent equal pairs across circular wraparound is invariant under all rotations.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy and State
hints.text: However, when rotations are viewed as linear sequences of length n, the pair formed across the boundary is split.

hints.title: Optimal Boundary and Processing
hints.text: Concatenate the sequence with itself to form a 2n array and count equal adjacent neighbors within windows of length n minus one.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
def countRotationsWithKAdjacentPairs(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    n = len(nums)
    if n <= 1:
        return 1 if k == 0 else 0

    extended = nums + nums
    # indicator of adjacent equals: match[i] = 1 if extended[i] == extended[i+1] else 0
    matches = [1 if extended[i] == extended[i + 1] else 0 for i in range(2 * n - 1)]

    # Each rotation of length n contains n - 1 adjacent pairs
    curr = sum(matches[:n - 1])
    ans = 1 if curr == k else 0

    for i in range(1, n):
        curr += matches[i + n - 2] - matches[i - 1]
        if curr == k:
            ans += 1
    return ans
```

complexity.notes: Sliding window of length n-1 over double-length array counts adjacent equal elements.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all rotations individually takes O(n^2) operations.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Indicator array of size 2n tracks adjacent matching pairs.
